subject.title: Feature Request: Masked Secrets - Prevent Agent from Accessing Raw API Keys

question: Should OpenClaw provide a native credential broker for approved tool execution, and what exact boundary must it guarantee against the general agent shell?
rationale: This determines whether credentials remain in-process, move behind tool-scoped injection, or stay an external plugin or service responsibility; implementation cannot safely define that guarantee without security-owner intent.

options.title: Native credential broker
options.body: Add a core security-owned broker with capability-scoped injection, non-agent-readable storage, exact redaction, and an explicit threat model.

options.title: Plugin contract only
options.body: Standardize security-reviewed credential-provider hooks while keeping secret storage and dispatch outside core.

options.title: Document external isolation
options.body: Keep the current core model and formally recommend OS or service isolation without promising native masking.

recommendation.title: Native credential broker
recommendation.body: Add a core security-owned broker with capability-scoped injection, non-agent-readable storage, exact redaction, and an explicit threat model.

likelyOwner.reason: The security ownership group is the best available owner for defining the credential trust boundary and acceptable guarantees.
